# Every theorem: the formula, and what Sierra's Better DFM does

<!-- Generated by leanvsdfm/tools/theorem_table.py from the Lean sources. Do not edit by hand. -->

<!-- THEOREMS:BEGIN -->
**97 theorems** in `leanvsdfm/LeanVsDFM/`, each one checked by the Lean 4 kernel. For every theorem: the formula with the real numbers, what it proves in plain words, and what Sierra Circuits' Better DFM does about the same thing.

**How to read the last column.** Better DFM takes Gerber RS-274X or ODB++ files, drill files and an optional IPC-356 netlist. You enter the minimum trace, minimum space, copper weight and minimum hole, and optionally the minimum annular ring and drill-to-copper. Its 40-point checklist covers signal, plane, solder mask, silkscreen and drill geometry, plus a netlist compare that finds opens and shorts. That description comes from [Sierra's Better DFM page](https://www.protoexpress.com/tools/pcb-dfm-tool/). **We did not run Better DFM on this board**: the board is placed, not routed, so there are no Gerbers to upload. We did not run Sierra's other tools either. Where one of them covers a claim, the column names it from that tool's own page: [BOM Checker](https://www.protoexpress.com/tools/bom-checker-tool/), [Stackup Designer](https://www.protoexpress.com/tools/pcb-stackup-designer/), [Impedance Calculator](https://www.protoexpress.com/tools/pcb-impedance-calculator/), [PDN Analyzer](https://www.protoexpress.com/tools/power-distribution-network-analyzer/).

Better DFM also checks things none of these theorems touch: annular ring, solder mask, silkscreen and drill-to-copper on the real Gerbers. Sierra also advertises DFA checks on turnkey assembly orders; that is a service on an order, not part of the Better DFM tool, and we did not examine it. The column answers one question only: for each thing Lean proves here, does Better DFM look at it?

| Answer in the last column | Meaning | Theorems |
|---|---|---:|
| **Checks this** | Better DFM tests the same thing. | 0 |
| **Checks part of this** | One part of the claim is a Better DFM check, the rest is not. | 1 |
| **Checks the geometry, not this claim** | A Better DFM check sees the related copper or pads, but it cannot decide the claim. | 9 |
| **Separate Sierra tool** | Not in Better DFM. Another Sierra tool covers the topic. | 9 |
| **Not in the DFM checklist** | Nothing in the 40-point checklist looks at it. | 78 |
| | | **97** |

<summary><b>Fixers.lean</b>: 30 theorems, search the buildable part values for one that meets the spec, and prove the answer</summary>

$E12$ = capacitor values 10 to 82 pF, $E24$ = resistor values 100 Ω to 9.1 kΩ. Crystal load: $C_L(c)=\lfloor c/2\rfloor+25$ in 0.1 pF (two equal capacitors in series plus 2.5 pF stray). LED current: $I(r)=\lceil\frac{1550\cdot10^{6}}{950r}\rceil$ µA (3.35 V supply, 1.8 V LED, resistor 5 % low). PLL: $f=\frac{12000F}{p_1p_2}$ kHz, legal when $16\le F\le320$, $750\le12F\le1600$ and $1\le p_2\le p_1\le7$. Regulator: $T_j(i)=50+\lceil\frac{250\cdot2000i}{10^{6}}\rceil$ °C at load $i$ mA (50 °C ambient, 250 °C/W, 2.0 V drop).

| Theorem | Formula | What it proves | What Sierra's DFM does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `find?_sound` | $\mathrm{find?}(p,l)=\mathrm{some}(a)\Rightarrow p(a)\land a\in l$ | Whatever a fixer's search returns meets the spec and comes from the list of buildable values. | **Not in the DFM checklist.** No counterpart: this is a proof about our own fixer. |
| `find?_first` | $\mathrm{find?}(p,l)=\mathrm{some}(a)\Rightarrow l=\mathrm{pre}\mathbin{++}(a::\mathrm{post})\land\forall b\in\mathrm{pre}:\neg p(b)$ | Every value the search skipped before its answer fails the spec, so the answer is the first that works. | **Not in the DFM checklist.** No counterpart: this is a proof about our own fixer. |
| `crystal_fails` | $C_L(220)=110+25=135$; $\lvert135-100\rvert=35\gt10$ (0.1 pF) | 22 pF load capacitors give the crystal 13.5 pF, outside 10 pF ± 1 pF. | **Not in the DFM checklist.** Capacitor values are not in fabrication files. |

| `crystal_sound` | $\mathrm{fix}(t)=\mathrm{some}(c)\Rightarrow\lvert C_L(c)-t\rvert\le10$ | For any target, whatever value the fixer returns meets the load spec. | **Not in the DFM checklist.** No counterpart: this is a proof about our own fixer. |

$Z$ is the set of six impedance nets named in the instructions: `USB_P`, `USB_N`, `USBR_P`, `USBR_N`, `D_P`, `D_N`. Lean's trace rule $\mathrm{rule}(n,w,s)$ is $(w,s)=(5,4)$ mil when $n\in Z$, and $w\ge6\land s\ge6$ mil for every other net. $I(r)$ is the LED current defined under Fixers.

| Theorem | Formula | What it proves | What Sierra's DFM does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `break1_only_row5` | $\lbrace l\in\mathrm{BOM}:\mathrm{qty}(l)\ne\lvert\mathrm{refdes}(l)\rvert\rbrace=\lbrace\text{row 5}\rbrace$ | Exactly one BOM row has a quantity that disagrees with its own designator list: row 5, the LEDs. | **Separate Sierra tool.** BOM Checker compares quantity with reference designators, so this is its kind of finding. Better DFM does not read the BOM. |
| `break1_row5` | $(\mathrm{qty},\lvert\mathrm{refdes}\rvert)=(8,7)$ for row 5 | Row 5 says 8 parts and lists 7 designators (D3 to D9). | **Separate Sierra tool.** BOM Checker compares quantity with reference designators, so this is its kind of finding. Better DFM does not read the BOM. |
| `break1_schematic_has_7_leds` | $\lvert\lbrace r\in\mathrm{schematic}:r\text{ starts with D}\rbrace\rvert=7$ | The schematic draws exactly 7 LEDs, so 7 is the right number. | **Not in the DFM checklist.** Neither Better DFM nor the BOM Checker takes the schematic as input. |
| `bom_schematic_sync` | $\mathrm{refs}(\mathrm{BOM})\subseteq\mathrm{refs}(\mathrm{sch})\land\mathrm{refs}(\mathrm{sch})\subseteq\mathrm{refs}(\mathrm{BOM})$ | Every BOM designator is on the schematic and every schematic part is on the BOM. | **Not in the DFM checklist.** Neither Better DFM nor the BOM Checker takes the schematic as input. |
| `break1_fixed` | $\mathrm{qty}'(l)=\lvert\mathrm{refdes}(l)\rvert$ makes every row $l$ consistent | After the fix every BOM row agrees with its designator list. | **Separate Sierra tool.** BOM Checker lets you correct the row by hand in its window. |
| `break1_fix_changes_only_row5` | $\lbrace(l,\mathrm{qty},\mathrm{qty}'):\mathrm{qty}\ne\mathrm{qty}'\rbrace=\lbrace(5,8,7)\rbrace$ | The fix changes one number only: row 5 from 8 to 7. | **Not in the DFM checklist.** No counterpart: this is a proof that our fix changes nothing else. |
| `break2_conflict` | $0.5\ne1.0$ (oz, stored as $5\ne10$ tenths) | The stack-up drawing (0.5 oz) and the instructions (1 oz) give different inner copper weights. | **Not in the DFM checklist.** It checks your files against the values you enter, not one document against another. |

Better DFM's checklist has no thickness check. |
| `external_copper_consistent` | $600+800+100=1500\ge1370$ (µin) | The outer layers as drawn (1.5 mil finished) are at least 1 oz (1.37 mil). | **Not in the DFM checklist.** Outer finished copper weight is a value you enter, not something it compares with another document. |
| `led_resistor_from_bom` | $\mathrm{value}(\text{row 13})=330$ | The LED resistor value used in the proofs is read from BOM row 13 (R12 to R18). | **Not in the DFM checklist.** BOM values are not in fabrication files. |
| `break3_default_drive_fails` | $I(330)=\lceil\frac{1550\cdot10^{6}}{950\cdot330}\rceil=4945\gt4000$ (µA) | With the BOM's 330 Ω, worst-case LED current exceeds the RP2040's default 4 mA pad drive. | **Not in the DFM checklist.** Current through a part is not a geometry check. |
| `break3_fixed_by_8mA` | $4945\le8000$ and $7\cdot4945=34615\le50000$ (µA) | Setting the pad drive to 8 mA makes the unchanged BOM value legal. | **Not in the DFM checklist.** Current through a part is not a geometry check. |
| `break3_alt_fix` | first $r\in E24$ with $I(r)\le4000$ and $7I(r)\le50000$ is $r=430$ | If the BOM could change, 430 Ω is the smallest E24 value that works at 4 mA. | **Not in the DFM checklist.** Its only automatic fixes are solder-mask and silkscreen adjustments. |

<details>
<summary><b>Fit3D.lean</b>: 4 theorems, 2D to 3D: courtyards, 3D bodies and collisions, for any board</summary>

All coordinates are integer nanometres, KiCad's own unit. A box is $(x_0,y_0,x_1,y_1)$. $a\subseteq A$ means $A.x_0\le a.x_0\land a.x_1\le A.x_1\land A.y_0\le a.y_0\land a.y_1\le A.y_1$. $\mathrm{sep}(a,b)$ is the separating-axis test $a.x_1\le b.x_0\lor b.x_1\le a.x_0\lor a.y_1\le b.y_0\lor b.y_1\le a.y_0$. $C_i$ is the courtyard of part $i$ (2D, from KiCad) and $B_i$ its body (3D, measured from the STEP model with OpenCascade). The outline test uses cross products: a point $(x,y)$ is inside a convex outline when $(b_x-a_x)(y-a_y)-(b_y-a_y)(x-a_x)$ has the same sign for every edge from $a$ to $b$.

| Theorem | Formula | What it proves | What Sierra's DFM does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sep_of_inside` | $a\subseteq A\land b\subseteq B\land\mathrm{sep}(A,B)\Rightarrow\mathrm{sep}(a,b)$ | If two courtyards do not overlap, nothing inside them overlaps either. | **Not in the DFM checklist.** Courtyards and 3D bodies are not among its signal, plane, mask, silkscreen and drill checks. |
| `sep_no_common_point` | $\mathrm{sep}(a,b)\Rightarrow\neg\exists(x,y):(x,y)\in\mathrm{int}(a)\cap\mathrm{int}(b)$ | Separated rectangles share no interior point. | **Not in the DFM checklist.** Courtyards and 3D bodies are not among its signal, plane, mask, silkscreen and drill checks. |
| `courtSep_pairwise` | $\mathrm{courtSep}(P)\Rightarrow\forall i\lt j:\mathrm{sep}(C_i,C_j)$ | If the checker's courtyard pass says yes, every pair of courtyards is separated. | **Not in the DFM checklist.** Courtyards and 3D bodies are not among its signal, plane, mask, silkscreen and drill checks. |
| `bodies_never_collide` | $(\forall i:B_i\subseteq C_i)\land\mathrm{courtSep}(P)\Rightarrow\forall i\lt j:\mathrm{sep}(B_i,B_j)$ | Main theorem: if the checker accepts a board, no two 3D part bodies overlap. It holds for any board. | **Not in the DFM checklist.** Courtyards and 3D bodies are not among its signal, plane, mask, silkscreen and drill checks. |

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>Report.lean</b>: 4 theorems, green, yellow, red: the overall verdict is the worst row</summary>

$\mathrm{rank}$: green $=0$, yellow $=1$, red $=2$. $\mathrm{worst}(a,b)$ is $a$ when $\mathrm{rank}(a)\ge\mathrm{rank}(b)$, otherwise $b$. $\mathrm{overall}(R)$ folds $\mathrm{worst}$ over the rows $R$ starting from green; $\mathrm{fold}(c,R)$ is the same fold starting from colour $c$.

| Theorem | Formula | What it proves | What Sierra's DFM does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `worst_ge_left` | $\mathrm{rank}(a)\le\mathrm{rank}(\mathrm{worst}(a,b))$ | Combining two colours never gives something better than the first. | **Not in the DFM checklist.** No counterpart: Better DFM emails a list of issues, not a combined verdict. |
| `worst_ge_right` | $\mathrm{rank}(b)\le\mathrm{rank}(\mathrm{worst}(a,b))$ | Nor better than the second. | **Not in the DFM checklist.** No counterpart: Better DFM emails a list of issues, not a combined verdict. |
| `overall_is_worst_aux` | $\mathrm{rank}(c)\le\mathrm{rank}(\mathrm{fold}(c,R))\land\forall r\in R:\mathrm{rank}(r)\le\mathrm{rank}(\mathrm{fold}(c,R))$ | Helper for the next theorem: folding the rows from any starting colour never loses a worse colour. | **Not in the DFM checklist.** No counterpart: Better DFM emails a list of issues, not a combined verdict. |
| `overall_is_worst` | $\forall r\in R:\mathrm{rank}(r)\le\mathrm{rank}(\mathrm{overall}(R))$ | The overall verdict is at least as bad as every row: one red row makes the board red. | **Not in the DFM checklist.** No counterpart: Better DFM emails a list of issues, not a combined verdict. |

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>Check.lean</b>: 4 theorems, one colour per component, never worse than the board's verdict</summary>

$\mathrm{comp}(R,c)$ is the colour of component $c$: the worst colour among the findings in the rows $R$ that name it. $\mathrm{board}(R)$ is the same for the findings that name no component. $\mathrm{fold}(c,X)$ folds $\mathrm{worst}$ over the list $X$ starting from colour $c$.

| Theorem | Formula | What it proves | What Sierra's DFM does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `worst_le` | $\mathrm{rank}(a)\le m\land\mathrm{rank}(b)\le m\Rightarrow\mathrm{rank}(\mathrm{worst}(a,b))\le m$ | If two colours are both no worse than a bound, neither is the worse of the two. | **Not in the DFM checklist.** No counterpart: Better DFM emails a list of issues, not a combined verdict. |
| `foldl_worst_le` | $\mathrm{rank}(c)\le m\land\forall x\in X:\mathrm{rank}(x)\le m\Rightarrow\mathrm{rank}(\mathrm{fold}(c,X))\le m$ | Folding any list of colours stays under a bound that every colour in the list respects. | **Not in the DFM checklist.** No counterpart: Better DFM emails a list of issues, not a combined verdict. |
| `comp_le_overall` | $\forall c:\mathrm{rank}(\mathrm{comp}(R,c))\le\mathrm{rank}(\mathrm{overall}(R))$ | No single component is ever shown worse than the overall verdict of the board. | **Not in the DFM checklist.** No counterpart: Better DFM emails a list of issues, not a combined verdict. |
| `board_le_overall` | $\mathrm{rank}(\mathrm{board}(R))\le\mathrm{rank}(\mathrm{overall}(R))$ | Nor is the bare board. | **Not in the DFM checklist.** No counterpart: Better DFM emails a list of issues, not a combined verdict. |

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>Verify.lean</b>: 11 theorems, verdicts on our KiCad board and on four boards with one planted mistake each</summary>

$B$ is the list of footprints read from `leanvsdfm/pcb/sierrathon.kicad_pcb` with KiCad's own API. $P$ is the same 54 parts with courtyards, pad boxes and 3D bodies. $\mathrm{verify}$ lists every finding: missing part, wrong package, wrong net, missing pad, stray net, LED polarity, land pattern. $\mathrm{electrical}$ keeps the errors and drops the two that are not (stand-in footprints and buildable variants).

| Theorem | Formula | What it proves | What Sierra's DFM does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `our_board` | $\mathrm{verify}(B)=[\text{J1},\text{SW1},\text{SW2},\text{SW3}]$, each a stand-in footprint | On our KiCad board every package, every schematic pin-to-net connection, LED polarity and the U3 land pattern verify. The only findings are four parts on library stand-in footprints. | **Not in the DFM checklist.** RS-274X Gerbers carry no part numbers, and no check in its list compares a footprint with a part. |
| `our_board_electrically_clean` | $\forall(r,p,n)\in\mathrm{pins}:\mathrm{net}(\mathrm{pad}(r,p))=n$; $\mathrm{electrical}(\mathrm{verify}(B))=\varnothing$ | No wrong package, wrong net, missing pad, stray connection, reversed LED or land-pattern error anywhere on our board. | **Checks the geometry, not this claim.** Netlist compare finds opens and shorts between the Gerbers and an IPC-356 netlist you upload, not a mismatch with the schematic. |
| `catches_narrow_flash` | $\mathrm{lib}(\mathrm{U3})=\text{SOIC-8 3.9 mm}\ne\text{SOIC-8 5.23 mm}=\mathrm{pkg}(\text{W25Q128JVSIQ})$ | A 150 mil SOIC-8 under the 208 mil flash is caught, although the footprint itself is clean. | **Checks the geometry, not this claim.** Sees pad spacing, mask and silkscreen on the footprint, not which part it is for. |
| `catches_reversed_led` | $\mathrm{net}(\mathrm{D5}.1)\ne\mathrm{GND}$ (found `LED3_A`); 5 findings | D5 placed backwards is caught: both pads on the wrong net and the cathode not on GND. | **Checks the geometry, not this claim.** Netlist compare uses the IPC-356 netlist you upload. Exported from this layout, it carries the same swap as the copper. |
| `catches_wrong_cap_size` | $\mathrm{lib}(\mathrm{C4})=0603\ne0402=\mathrm{pkg}(\text{GCM155R71C104KA55D})$ | An 0603 footprint on an 0402 BOM line is caught. | **Checks the geometry, not this claim.** Sees pad geometry only. An 0603 land pattern is legal copper. |
| `catches_swapped_flash_pins` | $\mathrm{net}(\mathrm{U3}.2)=D0\ne D1$ and $\mathrm{net}(\mathrm{U3}.5)=D1\ne D0$ (QSPI data); 4 findings | Flash data pins 2 and 5 swapped on the footprint are caught. | **Checks the geometry, not this claim.** Netlist compare uses the IPC-356 netlist you upload. Exported from this layout, it carries the same swap as the copper. |
| `our_board_fits` | $\mathrm{fit3d}(\mathrm{outline},P)=\varnothing$: $B_i\subseteq C_i$; $\mathrm{sep}(C_i,C_j)$; pads and bodies inside the outline; drill $\ge203200$ nm | On our board every body is inside its courtyard, no courtyards overlap, everything is inside the hexagonal outline and every drill is at least 8 mil. | **Checks part of this.** Hole size against the minimum you pick, and rout-to-copper spacing at the edge. Courtyards and 3D bodies are not in its checklist. |
| `our_board_bodies_never_collide` | $\forall i\lt j:\mathrm{sep}(B_i,B_j)$ over the 49 bodies | No two 3D part bodies overlap on our board: the general theorem applied to it. | **Not in the DFM checklist.** Courtyards and 3D bodies are not among its signal, plane, mask, silkscreen and drill checks. |
| `our_board_unmodelled` | $\lbrace p\in P:\mathrm{model}(p)=\mathrm{none}\rbrace=\lbrace\text{J1}\rbrace$ (mounting holes excluded) | The only part with no 3D body model is the USB-C connector J1. | **Not in the DFM checklist.** No check in its list involves 3D models. |
| `our_board_envelope` | $t=1511198$ and $h_{max}=4300000$, so $t+h_{max}=5811198$ (nm) | The board is 1.511 mm thick and the tallest body is 4.300 mm, so the assembled board is 5.811 mm high. | **Not in the DFM checklist.** No height or thickness check in its list. |
| `our_board_counts` | $\lvert P\rvert=54$; $\lvert\lbrace p\in P:\mathrm{model}(p)\ne\mathrm{none}\rbrace\rvert=49$ | All 54 parts are on the board model, 49 of them with a 3D body. | **Not in the DFM checklist.** It does not count parts. The BOM Checker compares quantities inside the BOM only. |

</details>
